title: Pop Changes for Piano: From Triads to Passing Chords
body:
This lesson is for a pianist who can play triads. It puts the chords of [the lesson on C, Am, F, G](pop-changes.qmd) on the keyboard: a left-hand root and a close-position chord in the right hand. Each step has a keyboard diagram, the chart and a grand staff, and the band plays along. **How to use the page.** Press ▶ on a chart and the band plays it four times after a one-bar count-in. The bar that is sounding lights up, on the chart and on the staff. Under every chord is its Roman numeral, which stays the same in every key. The strip at the bottom of the window sets the key, the feel, the tempo and the chord instrument, and you can change them while the band plays. Shaded bars are the ones that differ from the version named under the chart. ## 1. The basic chords **C, Am, F, G.** The keyboard diagram shows one lane for each chord: the left-hand root (square) and a right-hand chord above it. The staff under the chart shows the same notes: treble clef for the right hand, bass clef for the left.
## 2. Extensions **Cadd9, Am7, Fadd9, Gsus2.** The right hand keeps its shape and adds one note. Look for the 9 or the 7 in the diagram.
## 3. Passing chords **C, G/B | Am, C/G | F, F♯dim | G.** The left hand walks: C, B, A, G, F, F♯, G. Each right-hand chord changes only where it has to.
## 4. Secondary dominants **C, E7 | Am, C7 | F, D7 | G7.** The chord with the outside note leads by half step into the next bar.
## Where to go next - Move to another key with the strip and watch which keys the right hand lands on. - Try the same steps with [guide tones](guide-tones.qmd) in the right hand: only the 3rd and 7th of each chord.
